annotation.title_clean: Minnesota Statutes 182.6526 Warehouse Distribution Worker Safety
annotation.title_en: Minnesota Statutes 182.6526 Warehouse Distribution Worker Safety
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Minnesota Legislature (Office of the Revisor of Statutes)
annotation.summary_en: Minnesota statute regulating large warehouse distribution employers' productivity quotas: requires written quota disclosure, protects breaks, gives workers access to their work speed data, triggers investigations for high injury rates, and provides enforcement and a private right of action. Algorithmic monitoring is implicit; robots and AI are not mentioned.
key_provisions_or_claims: Employers must give written plain-language descriptions of each quota and notice before increases.
Quotas may not prevent meal, rest, prayer or restroom breaks or safety compliance.
Employees can request 90 days of personal and aggregated work speed data.
Injury rates 30% above NAICS average trigger commissioner investigation and monthly safety committee meetings.
Enforcement by the commissioner plus a private civil action within one year.
